answer: Occupancy is 12.5%. The launch asks for 32 KB of LDS per 64-thread workgroup, and each compute unit has 64 KB, so only two workgroups and four waves are resident per CU out of a possible thirty-two. Wave slots would allow sixteen workgroups and the register budget would allow nine, so LDS is roughly four times more restrictive than the next constraint. With four waves per CU there is very little to switch to while a memory access is outstanding, which is consistent with a kernel whose speed tracks compute-unit count and nothing else.

gpu_time_share.note: The kernel accounts for essentially all GPU time and its average matches the HIP-event median of 12.60 ms, so the host-side measurement boundary is not hiding overhead.

limitations: SUPERSEDED: the occupancy figures here were computed from launch geometry and a 64 KB per-CU pool. rocprofv3 OccupancyPercent has since measured them, and confirmed 12.5% for this footprint. See measured_confirmation below.
One kernel, one method, one part; the RDNA4 host has no profiler installed so the same measurement has not been repeated there.

Low occupancy is consistent with the observed scaling but is not proof of the cause; a counter-based bandwidth or stall analysis would be needed to close that. The intervention in results/hip_lds_ab.json is stronger evidence than this correlation.

measured_confirmation.verdict: The derived figure for this footprint was right, but the model behind it was not. See model_correction.

model_correction.was: workgroups per CU = floor(65536 / footprint), from the 64 KB per CU the agent advertises.
model_correction.now: workgroups per WGP = floor(131072 / footprint), halved to give waves per CU, treating the pool as 128 KB shared by the two compute units of a workgroup processor.
model_correction.why_it_went_unnoticed: The two models agree whenever the division lands on an even number of workgroups per WGP. Both footprints measured at the time, 32768 and 12288, did exactly that, so the wrong model produced two correct answers.
model_correction.what_exposed_it: A third footprint of 13312 bytes gives nine workgroups per WGP, an odd number the per-CU model cannot express. It predicted 25% and the counter measured 28.04%.
model_correction.status: The corrected model matches OccupancyPercent on all three footprints. It is recorded as the model that fits the counter, not as a claim about hardware internals read from a specification.

next_experiments: DONE, see results/hip_lds_ab.json: the footprint was cut from 32768 to 12288 bytes rather than halved, giving 31.25% occupancy instead of the 25% predicted here, and latency improved 1.70x to 2.13x on both parts with identical checksums. Note the return was sublinear: 2.5x occupancy bought about 2x.

Raise the workgroup from 64 threads so each LDS allocation serves more waves, which changes occupancy without changing the footprint. Not yet tried, and it may compound or conflict with the footprint change above.

PARTLY ANSWERED, see results/hip_lds_ab.json: the Pink path is not intrinsically slower. Both Pink and concat were forced to reserve the same worst-case LDS, so Pink's smaller aggregate (44 against 112) bought nothing. With the narrowed cap the paper's ordering is restored on gfx1151 and the gfx1201 inversion shrinks from 2.28 ms to 0.16 ms.

profiler.note: Profiled on the RDNA3.5 part because it is the machine with the ROCm profiler suite installed; the RDNA4 host has roc-obj tooling only.

question: Why is the fused kernel 1.7x to 4.3x slower than the paper's runtime numbers, and why does RDNA4 buy nothing beyond its compute units?
